# Power bank for flying

The main thing is that the bank must be **100 Wh or less** and go in your **carry-on, never checked luggage**. Within that limit, I'd pick one of these two:

**Best for most people: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W), $89.99**
- At about 74 Wh it's under the 100 Wh limit.
- It can charge a laptop and a phone, and it has a digital display.
- It has 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports, and it weighs about 451 g (roughly 1 lb).
- [Buy the Baseus Blade H1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)

**Best for iPhone-only top-ups: Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000 mAh, 45 W), $53.99 with code AM52**
- At about 37 Wh it's well under the limit.
- It has Qi2.2 magnetic wireless charging: 25 W on iPhone 16 and 17 (not the 16e), 15 W on iPhone 12 to 15.
- The code was last tested on 2026-10-24, so it may change.
- [Buy the Baseus PicoGo AM52](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)

Both are affiliate links, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. The source I found covers only these two models, so this isn't a broad comparison of every power bank. Its own figures also don't say what the Blade H1's ports deliver when several devices charge at once.

## Rules to know before you fly
- **Limit:** The FAA allows lithium-ion power banks up to 100 Wh each. Larger ones (101-160 Wh) need airline approval. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- **Carry-on only:** Spare batteries and power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals:** Keep it in its original packaging or a pouch so nothing short-circuits it.
- **Airlines can be stricter:** Southwest now limits each customer to **one** power bank (effective April 20, 2026). It also bars charging the bank from in-seat power and requires it to be visible while in use. It can't go in the overhead bin. ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters))
- **Check your airline:** Quantity and Wh limits vary, so look at your carrier's policy before you go.

If a bank gets hot, swells, or smokes, tell the crew right away. ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))
